newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index options slow, directionless.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Index options slow, directionless.

text.p: Trading in U.S. stock index options was subdued and largely directionless Thursday as investors focused on comments from Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, traders said.
"It's relatively quiet compared to yesterday," an S&P 500 index .SPX options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said. "Greenspan is talking and it's making the market go both up and down."
Greenspan was testifying before the Senate Finance Committee.
In afternoon trade, the SPX was up 6.74 at 779.24, a new session high.
March S&P 500 futures were ahead 4.30 points at 782.60. The contract traded between 777.50 and 783.30.
Traders pegged fair value in the futures at 3.35 points to cash, with buy programs seen at a premium of 5.00 points and sell programs at a premium of 1.80 points.
"There hasn't been a lot of direction," the options trader said, adding that most of the activity was being done in at-the-money options.
Among other stock indices, the Dow industrial average .DJI was up 36 points at about 6,777, having ranged between 6,741 and 6,789.
The S&P 100 index .OEX added 5.77 points to 764.17. It traded between 758.40 and 765.34.
"I haven't seen any big orders," a broker in Chicago said, adding that strong technology stocks and firm bond prices were supporting the broad stock market.
Traders said the 1996 fourth quarter advance gross domestic product (GDP) report, due Friday before the market open, was not likely to shake the market.
"I think they're going to wait to see what the FOMC does and react to that the next day," the trader at the CME said.
The Federal Reserve's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets on Tuesday and Wednesday next week, although a policy change is not widely expected.
Traders said volatilities in February index options slipped early in the session but were firming in the afternoon and that volatilities in the March series were firming.
They said the move in volatilities was not surprising ahead of the economic data Friday and the FOMC meeting next week.
Among individual options, the OEX February 760 put was the most active, with volume of about 9,585 contracts. The February 750 put traded about 4,780 and the February 725 put traded 4,630.
The OEX February 785 call was the most active call. About 4,140 contracts changed hands.

In the SPX options traded at the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE), a box was seen in the March 650 and March 675 contracts, with 1,200 contracts of the puts and calls in both strike prices traded. ((--G.Crawford, 312 408 8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com))
